Parco — Mobile Parking Platform

Mobile Mobility iOS / Android B2C 2024

Parco is a mobile parking platform that enables cashless, ticket-free, pay-per-minute parking across hundreds of cities in Germany and Austria. The product operates within complex municipal regulations while serving users in time-critical, high-stress urban contexts.

We focused on translating regulatory complexity into a clear, fast, and trustworthy end-to-end experience.

Problem space

Urban parking is defined by:

  • Fragmented city rules and pricing models
  • High cognitive load at the moment of use
  • User anxiety around time limits, fines, and overpaying

Most parking systems optimize for enforcement rather than user understanding.

Key product features

  • Start & stop parking sessions
  • Minutely billing: users only pay for actual parking time
  • Cashless payments (Apple Pay, Google Pay, PayPal, SEPA)
  • Visibility into parking availability and busyness
  • City-wide coverage across Germany & Austria
  • Smart reminders before parking expires
  • Navigation to parking area and final destination

Design approach

We shaped a parking experience that prioritizes speed, clarity, and user confidence, translating complex municipal parking rules into a simple mobile flow for real-world, time-pressured situations.

  • Simplified user flows for starting and stopping parking sessions
  • Designed for edge cases: overstay anxiety, unclear zones, and payment trust
  • Surfaced real-time parking availability to help users predict where to find a spot
  • Balanced legal and municipal constraints with consumer-grade UX standards
  • Defined a modern, playful visual tone to reduce stress in urban contexts

Unexpected interview outcome

The session screen started as one button. Billing was already per minute, so a duration felt unnecessary. Start when you arrive, stop when you leave, pay for the time in between. To me it was the neatest interaction we could offer, and I expected it to test well.

We built both that version and a dial that sets an expected duration, and put them in front of 20 potential customers and our main stakeholders. Every one of them chose the dial.

The one-button version: start when you arrive, stop when you leave

The dial version: set an expected duration, extend or end early

Three reasons came up:

  • Estimating how long you will park is the habit people already have. It is how every parking meter works.
  • They wanted to see what the parking would cost before committing to it.
  • They enjoyed it. The dial was the part of the prototype people kept playing with.

So we shipped the dial, with per-minute billing behind it. You set an expected duration and see the estimate up front, the app reminds you before it runs out, adding time is one tap, and ending early refunds the difference. People got the control they asked for without the overpayment they were used to from meters.

The simplest interaction was not the one people wanted to use. That was worth finding out before we built it.

User values

  • Reduced cognitive load. No meters, tickets, or guessing parking duration. Users stay in control at all times.
  • Fair pricing & trust. Minutely billing eliminates overpaying and increases confidence in the system.
  • Stress-free urban mobility. Visibility into availability and busyness helps users predict where to find a spot, reducing uncertainty and unnecessary circling.
  • Flexibility in unpredictable situations. One-tap extensions and reminders adapt to real-life delays.
